PrimeBuild Infrastructure Announces P12-Billion Expansion in Central Luzon

Engineering and construction firm PrimeBuild Infrastructure is set to invest P12 billion in expanding its operations across Central Luzon, company officials announced Wednesday. The expansion, which is slated to break ground in late August, will focus on new equipment yards, a training center, and an additional fabrication plant in Tarlac, aiming to serve rising demand from both government and private sector projects.

“We see Central Luzon as a growth corridor for infrastructure development,” said PrimeBuild President Manuel Carlos during the press briefing in San Fernando, Pampanga. “This investment will allow us to better support ongoing road, bridge, and commercial building projects across the region.”

The move comes as the Philippine government continues to prioritize infrastructure spending, with the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) allocating P890 billion for 2024 projects nationwide. Local contractors anticipate increased opportunities, especially in provinces such as Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, and Pampanga, where urbanization and logistics developments are accelerating.

The new fabrication plant in Tarlac is expected to create up to 600 direct jobs, with further employment in transport, logistics, and services. “We welcome this initiative, which aligns with our workforce development goals,” said Engineer Lucille Santos, Central Luzon regional director for the Philippine Constructors Association. “The dedicated training center is particularly significant, as it will help address the skills gap and prepare more locals for technical roles.”

Industry analysts say the expansion reflects growing confidence in the region’s economic outlook. “We’re seeing consistent investments in engineering and construction, a positive sign for local economies and supply chains,” said economic consultant Josemaria Reyes.

PrimeBuild Infrastructure said it aims to complete all new facilities by the second quarter of 2026.
